  "text": "He left the key where it was.

“What rest?” he called.

The boy appeared in the doorway carrying a shallow wooden drawer. There were spoons in it, a prescription bag, the red-handled scissors his wife kept upstairs.

“Put that down.”

“Here?”

“Where you found it.”

The boy glanced at the woman.

“It won't go back now,” she said.

He took the drawer from him. Underneath, in pencil, someone had written a date. Tomorrow's date. He rubbed it with his thumb and the last figure blurred.

“Who told you to take this?”

The boy held out his hands. Dust lay in the creases of his palms.

“I was only helping.”

The cupboard handle clicked against the wood. All three looked at it.

He had bought the handle because the old one caught his sleeve. There had been two in the packet. The spare was still in the drawer he was holding.

He shifted the scissors aside. There it was, wrapped in its little plastic sleeve.

The woman pushed the money closer to the edge of the table.

“For the damage,” she said.

He set the drawer on a chair and went to the cupboard. A screw lay on the floor beneath it. He bent to pick it up, grateful for something small enough to understand.

“Don't open it standing there,” the boy said.

He straightened without the screw.

Inside the cupboard, someone began turning the handle back the other way.

The woman moved him aside, not roughly, and placed one foot against the bottom of the door.

“Now,” she said to the boy. “Bring the rest.”"
